title: Structure, arrow, consequence: when history becomes an executable mechanism
summary: StructureArrowConsequenceIsLearnedMechanism turns a cross-repo intuition into a small falsifier. It separates reversal-even support S from reversal-odd temporal flux A, keeps short-lived eligibility E distinct from delayed consequence C, then freezes the learned object and asks whether it executes fresh route probes. In the committed 32-seed v0, reversing history leaves S unchanged and flips A exactly; reward reassignment leaves S and A unchanged while changing C; structure alone is chance on direction, S+A is perfect on direction but chance on value, shuffled consequence returns the fork to chance, and the frozen full mechanism scores 1.00 on held-out probes. The important correction is that these are transformation classes, not three literal boxes: C is symmetric yet can create a policy gradient, and S remains a hard topology mask even when its score term is ablated.

nodes.claim: Builds the smallest executable separation of reciprocal structure, time-reversal-odd history, local eligibility and delayed consequence, then freezes the result and tests whether those residues support held-out action.
nodes.survived: All three predeclared v0 gates pass in the constructed fork world: reversal gives S difference 0 and A sign-flip error 0; S-only direction is 0.50 while S+A is 1.00; reward reassignment leaves S and A unchanged; full rewarded-fork and full held-out accuracy are 1.00; shuffled consequence gives 0.46875 fork accuracy across 32 seeds; S+C retains value but scores 0.50 on interior direction; no illegal-edge choice or probe-time mutation was detected.
nodes.killed: The neat three-box story does not survive intact. A+C is numerically identical to S+A+C because S still supplies the hard legal-edge mask, and symmetric C can itself induce a behavioral arrow through a delayed-eligibility value gradient. The toy therefore does not establish a universal learning law, a unique S/A/C basis, general credit assignment, a biological mechanism or discovered algorithm.

edges.why: The new repository explicitly inherits the earlier split between reciprocal structure and skew/direction, but recasts it as a transformation test: S is reversal-even and A is reversal-odd rather than treating direction as something passive geometry already contains.

Rytmi supplies a measured example where preserving activity while scrambling within-cycle temporal order destroys ordered replay, motivating a distinct variable for temporal asymmetry rather than generic activation strength.

FunctionalArbors separates recent local eligibility from delayed soma consequence and shows that transporting reward is easier than assigning it causally; SAC keeps E and C separate for exactly that reason.

FlyBench's clicker-neuron branch gives the visible local example: temporal filters leave eligibility, sparse delayed clicks change survival/growth, and the same later test reads a different substrate after a different teaching history.

The negative developmental-spectral result is the direct warning against assuming that temporal history automatically becomes useful anatomy: its local resonator/resource/stigmergy rules failed to preserve alternating-versus-blocked order above seed variation, motivating an explicit signed and credited decomposition.

OperatorTime asks which operation is available now given resident history; SAC supplies one minimal way for past structure, direction and consequence to remain frozen enough to change the operation available at a later probe.

motifs.title: Learning can break different equivalences in history before the residue becomes executable
motifs.description: The synthesis separates three questions that older repositories often mixed: which interactions remain possible, which temporal histories differ under reversal, and which otherwise similar directed histories differ under later consequence. SAC's v0 shows these transformation classes can be isolated in a tiny frozen executor, while its own ablations also show the basis is not unique. The broader research question is whether richer systems expose comparable reversal-even, reversal-odd and consequence-sensitive coordinates under intervention, or whether an outside decoder should return NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.
